newsitem.title: EU: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MAY 19-26.
newsitem.headline: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MAY 19-26.

text.p: THE HAGUE - EU foreign ministers meet on inter-governmental conference (IGC) ahead of May 23 extra summit in Noordwijk (Tues).
BRUSSELS - EU internal market ministers meet (Tues).
BRUSSELS - European People's Party (EPP) hold summit, focusing on inter-governmental conference and preparation for June 16-17 Amsterdam EU summit (Weds).
BRUSSELS - European Commission regular weeekly meeting (Weds).
NOORDWIJK, Netherlands - EU heads of government hold extraordinary summit to give extra push to efforts to seal new EU treaty at Amsterdam summit (Fri).
MIDDELBURG, Netherlands - EU agriculture ministers informal meeting (begins Sun to May 27); focus on future of European dairy policy.
- EU institutions closed for Whit Monday holiday.

CARACAS (NEW ITEM) - EU-Latin America inter-parliamentary conference (to Thurs); focus on combatting drug trafficking and corruption as precondition for political stability and effects of globalisation on development. EP president Jose Maria Gil Robles and Latin American parliament president Juan Adolfo Singer to attend.
THE HAGUE - EU foreign ministers meet to discuss inter-governmental conference (IGC) ahead of extra May 23 Noordwijk summit (1500/1300 GMT). Venue: Foreign Ministry building.

BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU agriculture ministers meet (1500/1300 GMT) (and Weds). Agenda includes: olive sector reforms; beefmeat premium regimes; farm cooperative guarantees related to insolvency; EU position on forestry; veterinary and plant health equivalency accords; protection of animals during transport; residues and pesticides.

BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU internal market ministers meet (1000/0800 GMT). Agenda includes: legislative simplification; customs transit; approval of drug precursors accord with U.S.; improving awareness of EU law within legal profession; green paper on public markets; results of working groups on statutes of European society; electronic commerce initiative; medical in vitro devices; legislation on ionised foodstuffs.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Bjerregaard holds n/conf on swimming water (1215/1015 GMT).

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament legal affairs committee hearing on "Robert Schuman project - Action programme to improve awareness of Community law for the legal profession" (morning). Venue: EP, L04B01.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following European Parliament Committees meet:
Civil Liberties (Commissioner Papoutsis gives address on strengthening measures to combat sexual abuse and exploitation of children)
Budgetary Control (Commissioner Bonino and Court of Auditors members present auditors special report on EU humanitarian aid 1992-1995)

BRUSSELS - European Association of Consumer Electronic Manufacturers (EACEM) holds conference on "Technology and copyright" (1030/0830 GMT). Venue: Management Centre Europe. Contact: Peter Verhille, Entente International Communication (322) 502 1558.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime meeting on "Who wants EMU? The political economy of EMU in France, Germany and the UK" (1315/1115 GMT). Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.
BRUSSELS - World Tin Conference begins at 0900/0700 GMT (to May 22). Venue: Chateau du Lac. Contact: ITRI (44 1895) 272406.

PARIS - European Association of Securities Dealers (EASD) conference on "The new European stock market for growing companies" (0900/0700 GMT). Venue: Hotel Royal Monceau. Contact: EASD (322) 227 6565. 161417 DED:BC-DIARY-WEEKLY =2 Reuter EC Report Weekly Diary (page 2/3 - Wednesday)
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EU agriculture ministers continue meeting, celebrating European Tree Day by planting tree in the press room at 1800/1600 GMT.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission regular weekly meeting (0900/0700 GMT). Provisional agenda includes:
- Commissioner Bangemann on telecoms numbering policy.
- Commissioner Fischler on Objective 5 for Spain.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission seminar on Agenda 2000.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European People's Party (EPP) summit (1800/1600 GMT); focus on inter-governmental conference (IGC) and preparation for Amsterdam EU summit. Participants include: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar, Irish Prime Minister John Bruton, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker, Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, European Commission President Jacques Santer, EP president Jose Maria Gil Robles and EPP president Wilfried Martens. Venue: Prieure de Val Duchesse. Contact: Marianne Amsoons (322) 284 2233.

BRUSSELS - MEP Jaak Vandemeulebroek hosts conference on "The EU ban on hormonal meat is based on valid scientific data" (1500/1300 GMT). N/conf 1030/0830 GMT. Venue: EP, Belliard 1. Contact: Bart Staes (322) 284 2394.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EP-Estonia Parliamentary meeting (1500/1300 GMT) (and Weds). Estonian European Affairs Minister Veldemann and European Commissioner van den Broek to attend.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament subcommittee on monetary affairs hearing on the "Introduction of the euro and tourism" (1000/0800 GMT). Venue: EP, MAE 2.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following European Parliament Committees meet:
Civil Liberties (Dutch Justice Minister Winnie Sorgdrager attends)
Institutional Affairs (Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini attends at 1000/0800 GMT
Transport (Commissioner Kinnock gives address on telematics, research, TEN corridors)
Development (public hearing on "The World Trade Organisation (WTO) and develooping countries")
Economic (Dutch State Secretary for Foreign Affairs Michiel Patijn attends at 1700/1500 GMT).

BRUSSELS - Club de Bruxelles conference on "Sustainable management of forests and derivative products in Europe and the rest of the world - What should European policy be?" (0900/0700 GMT) (to Friday). Speakers include: European Commissioners Bjerregaard, Fischler, de Deus Pinheiro; Dutch Farm Minister Jozias van Aartse; Finnish Agriculture Minister Kalevi Hemila; European Parliament deputies Juan Luis Colino and Ken Collins. Venue: Management Centre Europe, 118 rue de l'Aqueduc. Contact: Club de Bruxelles (322) 743 1520.

BRUSSELS - European Road Safety Federation (ERSF) n/conf to launch five-year medium-term programme on non-legislative activities for road safety in the EU in context of communication on road safety recently adopted by European Commission (1315/1115 GMT). Venue: Swissotel. Contact: Sandrine Poelmans, ERSF (322) 282 0828.

BRUSSELS - Belgian Association for Environment Rights conference on "Citizens and association rights in European environmental law" (0845/0645 GMT). Venue: SAS Radisson Hotel. Contact: Belgian Association for Environment Rights (32) 9 264 6926.
BRUSSELS - World Fuels Conferences conference on "Fuel quality and vehicle technology" (to Friday). Venue: Conrad Hotel. Contact: World Fuels Conferences (1) 703 812 0902.

LONDON - Agra Europe conference on "The Common Agricultural Policy" (0900/0800 GMT). Venue: Mayfair Inter-Continental. Contact: Agra Europe (44) 1892 511807. 161424 DED:BC-DIARY-WEEKLY =3 Reuter EC Report Weekly Diary (page 3/3 - Thurs-Sun)
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EP-Estonia parliamentary meeting (0900/0700 GMT) (2nd of two days). European Parliament president Jose Maria Gil-Robles gives address at 1030/0830 GMT.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament budget committee round-table on financial consequences of enlargement (0900/0700 GMT). Agenda includes: legislative and macroeconomic aspects, political institutions and audit bodies, public administrations. European Commissioner Liikanen and Court of Auditors Representative Everard to attend.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following European Parliament Committees meet:
Economic (Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt attends at 1100/0900 GMT)

BRUSSELS - British Chamber of Commerce in Belgium conference on "A time for change: The effect of the euro on new and existing stock exchanges and the presentation of the AIM (Alternative Investment Market)" (1400/1200 GMT). Venue: Auditorium Societe General, 30 rue Royale. Contact: British Chamber of Commerce in Belgium fax (322) 512 8363.
NOORDWIJK - EU heads of state hold extraordinary summit to give an extra push to efforts to seal a new EU treaty at the Amsterdam summit on June 16-17

BRUSSELS - ECARE (European Studies Institute, Free University of Brussels) conference on "Europe, East Asia, APEC and Asia-Europe meeting (ASEM) process" (0930/0730 GMT). Agenda includes: the future of regionalism in Europe and the Pacific; Europe, East Asia and Asia Pacific and Economic Cooperation (APEC): trade issues; beyond trade liberalisation: investment and strategic policy; Europe, East Asia and APEC: a shared global agenda? Venue: Sociology Institute, 44 avenue Jeanne. Contact: Romy Genin (322) 650 4138.

BRUSSELS - European Institute of Public Affairs and Lobbying (EIPAL) conference on "Practice and legal restrictions on lobbying the European institutions" (1400/1200 GMT). Venue: European Parliament. Contact: Glacomo Scuart, EIPAL (322) 481 7325.

MIDDELBURG, Netherlands (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU agriculture ministers hold informal meeting (To May 27). Focus on future of European dairy policy. Press opportunity at 1730/1530 GMT; on Tuesday closing news conference at 1230/1030 GMT.
